next_step: Run 2-week PoC with synthetic spike tests; finalize SLA and QPS targets
notes:
Overview: BeaconPulse is a cloud-native contact center platform used by mid-market retailers and delivery ops. Exploring Redwood for agent-assist + ticket summarization to reduce AHT and avoid manual escalation during extreme traffic spikes. Primary concern: reliability under bursts (Black Friday/holiday spikes + incident-driven callbacks).

Why Redwood: they want predictable latency and throughput during short windows of 10-30x baseline traffic; prefer reserved capacity or private deployment. Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to trade some cost for guaranteed latency SLAs.

SLA targets / Sizing asks:
- Agent-assist latency: p95 < 250ms for token generation (interactive assist)
- Ticket summarization: batch throughput target 2k tickets/min during peak ingest windows
- Sustained baseline qps: 800 req/s; planned spike profile: bursts to 5k concurrent requests for 2-6 hour windows
- Concurrency: up to 3k active agent sessions during peak; need KV cache warmup strategy

Reliability & fallback requirements:
- Automated routing to lower-cost quantized model when primary capacity saturated
- Graceful degradation: prioritization rules (live agent assist > outbound summarization > analytics)
- Circuit-breaker + retry policies, backpressure signals surfaced in console
- Require cold-start/scale benchmarks and cold-cache impact analysis

Security / Compliance:
- Must pass SOC2 and SSO/SAML integration; KMS for key control; audit logs retained 2 years for core flows; data residency: EU for EU customers

PoC plan (agreed with AE/SE):
- Week 0: security questionnaire submitted (see Drive).
- Week 1: sandbox deploy (private control plane + VPC peering).
- Week 2: synthetic spike run 1 (10x baseline, 2 hours). Capture latency, token cost, model fallback events.
- Week 3: synthetic spike run 2 (25x baseline, 4 hours) + failure injection (simulate DB latency causing ticket backlog).
- Week 4: review with infra & security, incorporate recommendations from Redwood Optimize.

Notes from calls / quotes:
- 2026-02-25 kickoff call (ff_20260225_1z9k): "If we lose assist responsiveness during promos we get large CSAT hits — can't have that."
- 2026-03-03 tech deep-dive (ff_20260303_x4b2): SE requested per-token cost model for fallback combos; BeaconPulse asked about KV cache persistence across model rollouts.

Open technical concerns:
- How Redwood handles very short high-magnitude bursts (<= 6 hours) without overprovisioning full-time capacity; need autoscale + burst credits model.
- Cold-cache penalties for agent assist when a new campaign starts; require quick KV-warm strategies.
- End-to-end observability: must show per-route token cost during spikes and queue backlog metrics.

Next steps / immediate asks:
- Redwood SE to provide sample load-test plan and expected cost delta for dedicated pool + burst capacity (requested by 2026-03-12).
- Security team to review questionnaire answers and confirm KMS/HSM integration timeline.
- BeaconPulse to provide access to a replay of a past spike (anonymized) for realistic load generation.

CRM timeline (recent activity):
- 2026-01-20: Initial inbound from BeaconPulse (form + usage profile).
- 2026-02-02: Demo of hosted API + dedicated options (AE: Maya).
- 2026-02-25: PoC kickoff call, captured in Fireflies (ff_20260225_1z9k).

Decision factors: predictable latency under bursts, strong observability for backpressure, and clear fallback/priority behavior. Procurement timeline tied to PoC results and security sign-off.
